Team — draft language below for inclusion in Exhibit C. I tried to keep it narrow and objective: 

1) Quarterly True-ups and Retroactivity: "Customer and Redwood will reconcile actual usage to committed usage on a quarterly basis (the "True-up"). Except where a material underreporting is discovered (defined as Customer underreporting aggregate usage by more than five percent (5%) in a calendar quarter based on an audit described below), no retroactive True-up shall be applied beyond the two (2) most recent completed quarters. Material underreporting discovered by Redwood during an audit shall be subject to retroactive adjustment for the period under audit only."

2) Overage Multiplier Base: "Overage charges, where applicable, shall be calculated as a multiplier of the per-token list rate (i.e., before application of any volume or term discounts set forth in the Order Form). The multiplier for monthly usage that exceeds the Maximum Band is two (2.0) times the per-token list rate unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties."

3) Credit Scheduling: "If, following a True-up, Customer is assessed additional fees and Customer timely schedules a capacity review with Redwood within thirty (30) days of notice of such fees, Redwood will, at its option, apply a credit equal to up to one (1) month of Customer's then-current Minimum Monthly Commitment. Such credit may be applied as a single credit or pro-rated across the two (2) subsequent invoices, subject to Redwood's right to withhold application of credits for any invoices that are more than thirty (30) days overdue."

Notes: the 5% threshold gives Redwood a bright-line to avoid chasing small reporting diffs; multiplier base on list rate keeps math simple for invoicing; credit schedule language supports Orchid's ask while preserving Redwood's collections rights.

Laura — if this looks acceptable commercially I recommend we: (a) update Exhibit C with the three clauses; (b) create a separate short SOW-style "capacity review" task so Orchid can trigger the review without re-opening commercial terms; and (c) ask finance to prepare a one-line memo showing net ARR impact under Orchid's forecast so sales has an approval record.
